investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T15:02–15:09Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") could not progress past agent creation, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was unschedulable for 145s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151088, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-08T15:04:37.451Z — the check ran to near-timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, confirming the agent creation call never completed.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, consistent with the pod never reaching a schedulable state.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=151338, status=fail — the state check also could not schedule a pod.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=149840, status=fail — the runtime check also could not schedule a pod.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885 — the remote machine type is what triggers kata.peerpods.io/vm scheduling.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently constrained to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size. If those 2 nodes are at capacity for any reason, all remote-agent creation fails.

Tertiary — a stuck or leaked remote-agent pod from a prior eval run is holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and was not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1883), reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence — transient cloud-provider quota limit on the underlying VM type used by kata peer-pods, causing the node resource to report as insufficient even if slots appear available in the node allocatable spec.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable=0 on all nodes (not just insufficient), the cause would be a misconfigured or missing device plugin rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the scheduler message disappears on a re-run immediately after this failure without any operator intervention, the cause is transient (e.g., a competing pod was deleted), not sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 2 nodes that carry kata.peerpods.io/vm show zero allocated VM slots at the time of failure, the root cause shifts to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration that prevents the pod from targeting those nodes.

If a code change in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs caused the runner to submit an incorrect node selector or resource request, the infrastructure may have capacity but the pod spec is malformed — this would be disproved by confirming the pod spec matches a previously working configuration.

If passing sibling checks exist for remote-agents in the same run window, the failure would be localized to a specific check's pod spec rather than a cluster-wide capacity problem — no passing siblings are present in this packet, which supports the cluster-wide diagnosis.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that verifies no orphaned or stuck remote-agent pods are present in the cluster before each remote-agent-create run, catching cleanup failures from prior runs.
Add a node-pool health eval that confirms the expected number of nodes matching the remote-agent affinity/selector are Ready and have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity.

Consider adding a latency-band eval that alerts at the warningLatencyMs threshold (240000ms) with a partial evidence snapshot, so capacity pressure is visible before the full outageLatencyMs (360000ms) timeout is reached.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating zero schedulable nodes: 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, while the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. This left 0/6 nodes available to schedule the remote-agent pod. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes and preemption is not applicable on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~143–145 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence payload and a full contract gap for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — the most directly supported cause, stated verbatim in the scheduler message (failed-check.message). No preemption victims were available, meaning all VM slots are in active use or reserved.

Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod template is too restrictive — 4 of 6 nodes are excluded entirely, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes and making quota exhaustion more likely.
Cluster autoscaler has not yet added a new node with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, or autoscaling is disabled or misconfigured for this node pool, leaving the 2 eligible nodes as the only supply.
A concurrent spike in remote-agent provisioning (by other users or eval runs) consumed all available VM slots before this eval's pod could be scheduled.
The node pool that carries kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was recently scaled down, drained, or had nodes removed, reducing available VM slots from a previously sufficient level.

If the remote-agent-state eval passes on the next scheduled run without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in concurrent VM usage) rather than a sustained capacity shortfall.

Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any runtime evidence, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature had no schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads at the time of the eval run. Of the 6 available nodes, 2 that support the kata peer-pods VM resource type had that resource exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes and preemption is not applicable on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T15:02–15:09Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") could not progress past agent creation, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' — pod was unschedulable for 145s before the check timed out.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151088, status=fail, endedAt=2026-07-08T15:04:37.451Z — the check ran to near-timeout without producing any evidence.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, confirming the agent creation call never completed.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, consistent with the pod never reaching a schedulable state.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=151338, status=fail — the state check also could not schedule a pod.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=149840, status=fail — the runtime check also could not schedule a pod.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885 — the remote machine type is what triggers kata.peerpods.io/vm scheduling.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently constrained to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size. If those 2 nodes are at capacity for any reason, all remote-agent creation fails.

Tertiary — a stuck or leaked remote-agent pod from a prior eval run is holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and was not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1883), reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence — transient cloud-provider quota limit on the underlying VM type used by kata peer-pods, causing the node resource to report as insufficient even if slots appear available in the node allocatable spec.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable=0 on all nodes (not just insufficient), the cause would be a misconfigured or missing device plugin rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the scheduler message disappears on a re-run immediately after this failure without any operator intervention, the cause is transient (e.g., a competing pod was deleted), not sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 2 nodes that carry kata.peerpods.io/vm show zero allocated VM slots at the time of failure, the root cause shifts to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration that prevents the pod from targeting those nodes.

If a code change in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs caused the runner to submit an incorrect node selector or resource request, the infrastructure may have capacity but the pod spec is malformed — this would be disproved by confirming the pod spec matches a previously working configuration.

If passing sibling checks exist for remote-agents in the same run window, the failure would be localized to a specific check's pod spec rather than a cluster-wide capacity problem — no passing siblings are present in this packet, which supports the cluster-wide diagnosis.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that verifies no orphaned or stuck remote-agent pods are present in the cluster before each remote-agent-create run, catching cleanup failures from prior runs.
Add a node-pool health eval that confirms the expected number of nodes matching the remote-agent affinity/selector are Ready and have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity.

Consider adding a latency-band eval that alerts at the warningLatencyMs threshold (240000ms) with a partial evidence snapshot, so capacity pressure is visible before the full outageLatencyMs (360000ms) timeout is reached.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating zero schedulable nodes: 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, while the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. This left 0/6 nodes available to schedule the remote-agent pod. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes and preemption is not applicable on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~143–145 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence payload and a full contract gap for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-08 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any runtime evidence, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature had no schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads at the time of the eval run. Of the 6 available nodes, 2 that support the kata peer-pods VM resource type had that resource exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes and preemption is not applicable on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: the contract at lines 266-270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these could be satisfied without a running agent pod.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latencyMs=149840 is well within the outage threshold, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling error, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the peer-pods-capable nodes are occupied by existing agent pods or other workloads, leaving no room for the eval's new pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or if node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool is smaller than the total cluster size.

[Possible] Cluster under-provisioning or missing scale-out: the cluster has only 2 nodes capable of running kata peer-pods VMs and no auto-scaling triggered (or auto-scaling was too slow) to add capacity before the eval's scheduling timeout.

[Possible] Leaked or stuck agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) from a previous run did not complete, those pods may still hold VM resource allocations, reducing available capacity for new scheduling attempts.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 eligible cluster nodes immediately to determine current capacity and identify which pods are consuming the VM slots.
Check for leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs in the eval namespace; if found, terminate them to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and re-run the eval to confirm recovery.

Review the node affinity and node selector configuration for remote-agent pods against the labels on all 6 cluster nodes to determine whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional or the result of label drift that is unnecessarily constraining the schedulable pool.

Assess whether the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have sufficient VM slot capacity for concurrent eval runs plus any production workloads; if not, evaluate adding more peer-pods-capable nodes or increasing the VM resource limit on existing nodes.

Re-run the eval after any capacity or cleanup action to confirm that all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are returned and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false in features.json (line 185), but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183–184); prioritize restoring scheduling capacity for the required checks first.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If node labels drifted or affinity rules changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk, making VM exhaustion more likely even at normal load.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and unallocated on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., a quota policy, admission webhook rejection, or node taint) would need to be investigated.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes were found to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the pod's node affinity/selector was intentionally correct, the problem would be localized purely to the 2-node capacity limit rather than any affinity misconfiguration.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and produced all 5 required evidence fields, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If prior eval runs show a consistent pass history for remote-agent-create and the cluster node count or VM slot count had not changed, it would suggest a sudden increase in concurrent workloads consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots rather than a configuration change.

If the withCleanup mechanism in run-status-probes.mjs is confirmed to have completed successfully for all prior runs (no leaked pods), leaked-pod resource consumption would be ruled out as a contributing cause.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a capacity-specific message if headroom is below a minimum threshold.

Add an eval that detects and reports leaked remote-agent pods (pods in the eval namespace older than a configurable TTL that were not cleaned up by withCleanup), to surface resource leaks before they exhaust scheduling capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules meets a minimum count, alerting if label drift reduces the schedulable pool below the expected size.
Consider a historical baseline eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization over time so that gradual capacity erosion is detected before it causes a full scheduling failure.
